messages.content: What are my rights as a tenant in the state of Texas?

message.content:
Below is an overview of key tenant rights under Texas law (as of the latest statutes and regulations). This isn’t legal advice, but it summarizes the most common protections you have when renting a home or apartment in Texas. | Area | What You’re Generally Entitled To | |------|-----------------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit and two months’ rent for an unfurnished unit.
• The deposit must be returned within 30 days after you move out, minus any lawful deductions (e.g., unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear). | | **Notice Requirements** | • For month‑to‑month leases: 30‑day written notice to terminate.
• For fixed‑term leases: landlord must give at least 30 days’ notice before the lease ends if they intend not to renew.
• If the landlord wants to increase rent, they must give 30 days’ written notice before the new rate takes effect. | | **Habitability & Repairs** | • Landlords must keep the premises in a safe, livable condition—plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, pest control, etc.
• If repairs aren’t made promptly, you may withhold rent (in some cases) or pursue a “repair‑and‑deduct” remedy. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlords cannot enter your unit without proper notice (usually 24 hours) unless there’s an emergency. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Under federal Fair Housing laws and Texas Civil Rights Act, landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or other protected classes. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlords must follow the formal eviction procedure: serve a written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for nonpayment), file a complaint in court, attend a hearing, and obtain a judgment before a sheriff can enforce removal. | | **Lease Terms & Modifications** | • Any changes to the lease must be in writing and signed by both parties. Oral agreements are generally enforceable only if they meet the statute of frauds (e.g., contracts that cannot be performed within one year). | | **Rent Control & Rent Increases** | • Texas has no statewide rent‑control law; however, local ordinances may impose limits in certain cities (e.g., Austin, Houston). Check city codes. | | **Subletting & Assignment** | • Many leases allow subletting or assignment with landlord approval. If the lease prohibits it, you may still sublet if the landlord refuses to let you assign the lease. | | **Legal Remedies** | • If a landlord violates your rights, you can file a complaint with the Texas Attorney General’s Office, the local housing agency, or sue in small claims court (up to $20,000). | ### Practical Steps If You Think Your Rights Are Violated 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of all communications, receipts, photos of damages, and a log of repair requests. 2. **Serve Written Notice** – If you’re withholding rent or requesting repairs, send a certified letter or email with a read receipt. 3. **File a Complaint** – Contact the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) or your local housing authority. 4. **Seek Legal Aid** – Free or low‑cost services are available through community legal aid organizations (e.g., Texas Legal Services Center). ### Useful Resources | Resource | Link | |----------|------| | Texas Property Code (full text) | https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/PC/htm/PC.htm | | TDHCA – Tenant Rights | https://www.tdhca.state.tx.us/ | | Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection | https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/consumer-protection | | Local Housing Authority (search by city) | https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/housing/sfh/hfa | --- If you’d like a sample lease or a more detailed contract tailored to your situation, just let me know what type of agreement you need (e.g., residential lease, commercial lease, sublease) and I can generate a draft for you.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are my rights as a tenant in the state of Texas?" They want information about tenant rights. We can provide general info. But we might also offer to generate a contract. The user didn't ask for a contract. So no need to call the function. Just answer. Provide overview: security deposit limits, notice requirements, habitability, eviction process, etc. Also mention resources. No policy violation.
